cards.text: The prophet Micah just painted a gorgeous future: nations beating their swords into plowshares, and the LORD gathering the outcast (Micah 4:3, 6). Then the message turns to the Daughter of Zion (Zion is Jerusalem) and talks about RIGHT NOW. Right now she's crying aloud, and the message asks her why: is there no king among you, has your counselor perished?

cards.question: Anguish is gripping the Daughter of Zion. What does the prophecy say she's like?

cards.text: Writhe in agony like a woman in labor, the message tells the Daughter of Zion, because she'll leave the city and camp in the open fields. Then she'll go to Babylon.

cards.question: True or false: the prophecy says that in Babylon, the LORD will redeem the Daughter of Zion from the hand of her enemies.

cards.text: The LORD got ME out of the back of a JUNK DRAWER, friend, so He can handle Babylon. But right now, many nations have assembled against Zion, saying, “Let her be defiled, and let us feast our eyes on Zion.”

cards.question: True or false: the prophecy says the nations gathered against Zion understand the LORD's plan.

cards.text: Here's the twist: the LORD has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor. They wanted to feast their eyes on Zion, friend, and that's like walking into a bakery to watch the show and finding out YOU'RE the dough.

cards.question: The LORD has gathered the nations like sheaves. What does the prophecy tell the Daughter of Zion to do?

cards.text: And she'll get the gear for the job: horns of iron and hooves of bronze to break many peoples to pieces. Iron AND bronze, friend, and I can't even win a fight with a sticky oven door.

cards.question: After the Daughter of Zion breaks many peoples to pieces, what does the prophecy say she'll do with their wealth?

cards.text: Back to now: mobilize your troops, for a siege is laid against us. With a rod they will strike the cheek of the judge of Israel.

Then the message turns to a little town, small among the clans of Judah. Out of it will come One to be ruler over Israel, which is like the tiniest bakery on the block, ONE oven and a handwritten sign, landing the ROYAL order.

cards.question: Which small town in Judah will this ruler over Israel come from?
Bethlehem is small, but how far back does the prophecy say this ruler's origins go?

answers.text: From the days of King Saul
From the days of the judges

cards.text: So Israel will be abandoned until she who is in labor has given birth.

cards.question: Once she who is in labor gives birth, the prophecy says the rest of the ruler's brothers will ___ to the children of Israel.

cards.text: And here's what this ruler will do: stand and shepherd His flock.

cards.question: True or false: the prophecy says the ruler from Bethlehem will shepherd His flock in the strength of the LORD.
With the ruler from Bethlehem shepherding the flock, how does Micah say His people will live?

cards.text: He'll shepherd in the majestic name of the LORD His God, and His greatness will reach to the ends of the earth, the WHOLE map, friend, while my whole planet is just big enough for one bakery. Then Micah names a real threat: Assyria, whose king captured Samaria (2 Kings 17:6), invading the land and trampling its citadels.

cards.question: When Assyria invades and tramples our citadels, Micah says the ruler from Bethlehem will be our ___.

cards.text: Against Assyria, Micah says, “We will raise against it seven shepherds, even eight leaders of men.” EIGHT leaders, friend, and the closest thing to leadership in my junk drawer was the dead batteries arguing over who had the most charge left!

cards.question: True or false: Micah says the seven shepherds and eight leaders raised against Assyria will flee from its land.

cards.text: They'll rule the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod, the mighty hunter before the LORD (Genesis 10:9), with the blade drawn. So He will deliver us when Assyria invades our land and marches into our borders.
